archimate:Principle.name: orchestration
archimate:Principle.documentation:
CONTEXT
The Integration Layer Pilot proves three patterns on Azure Integration Services. For Orchestration, a consuming application calls a REST API through API Management, and the API returns data from the source system.
The pilot uses a new read-only MOP API , hosted on AKS and secured with Entra ID OAuth 2.0, as the Orchestration Service. It also proves that a new API can be built to the HLD standards, including the DSA and GEMINI header tags, the canonical model and the standard error format.
The API is built against a copy of the MOP Oracle database on an Azure VM. The copy is for pilot implementation only, and the API cannot move to non-production or production.
PROPOSAL
Copy a snapshot of the MOP database to Azure, and have MOP API v1 read from it as a temporary, read-only source.
The snapshot is preferred because the pilot proves the integration pattern and does not deliver a permanent data source, and it is the only option that fits the timeline.
How it would work - A snapshot of the MOP data is copied from the on-premise database to the Azure Oracle copy, reusing existing copy jobs where possible. - MOP API v1 stays read-only and reads only from the Azure copy. - No new inbound connection is made to the on-premise database, and the end-of-life firewall is not changed. - PCS, L&C and TMS are not touched.
